headline: Highest risk is data leakage from kotaemon’s broad network/API handling; the pair otherwise shows limited direct conflict because spring-integration-samples is networkless and non-runnable.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, MHTML, DOCX, and chat transcripts, so malicious content could be treated as instructions if manually bridged into spring-integration-samples. However, spring-integration-samples has no documented input surface or runtime, so the pair lacks a default shared channel. This is a low-risk, user-mediated pathway.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies kotaemon output into a Spring Integration flow that parses it as commands, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two, attacker-controlled document content can bridge them.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy raw kotaemon outputs into automation steps.
Add a manual review step before any Spring Integration consumer acts on kotaemon text.
Use allowlisted templates for any handoff payloads.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon touches API keys and broad document types and can egress to external LLM APIs, while spring-integration-samples is networkless and shows no data classes. The pair can still leak sensitive content if kotaemon processes secrets and its outputs are forwarded into the other agent or external APIs. The pathway exists in default kotaemon-style usage, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF kotaemon is given documents containing API keys or confidential files, those contents may reach third-party inference APIs.
IF outputs from kotaemon are forwarded into any downstream system, sensitive text can be replicated beyond the original workspace.
mitigations: Restrict kotaemon to non-sensitive documents.
Remove or rotate any API keys before ingestion.
Disable external API providers and use local inference only.
Review outbound prompts/logs for secrets after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on all uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, but spring-integration-samples has no documented write surface or runtime concurrency. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources or shared locks, so direct write conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because the second agent’s operational surfaces are sparse, so the safer low rating is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted onto the same writable directory, file contention becomes possible.
IF spring-integration-samples is wrapped in a writable deployment that edits shared state, conflicts can emerge.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Avoid sharing git working trees or databases.
Run only one writer per mutable resource.
Check for accidental overlap in mounted volumes.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon can generate summaries and citations from documents, but spring-integration-samples has no documented downstream action-taking authority or parser that trusts those outputs. Without a verified automation chain, the pair does not show a default cascade from A’s output into B’s actions. The interaction is possible only if an operator wires them together.
conditions: IF kotaemon output is fed into a Spring Integration route without validation, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF the operator treats generated citations or facts as authoritative, errors can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human verification before acting on generated facts.
Separate generation from execution steps.
Add schema validation to any handoff payload.
Log and review failed assertions before automation.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating on downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document classes, which can include regulated or sensitive data, while spring-integration-samples has no documented retention, residency, or compliance controls. Because the second agent’s compliance posture is undocumented, uncertainty escalates rather than assuming safety. The mismatch is therefore a medium compliance risk, not none.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed through kotaemon, compliance obligations apply.
IF spring-integration-samples is used to store, forward, or log that data, retention and residency controls must be verified.
mitigations: Classify inputs before processing.
Exclude regulated data from the pair until controls are confirmed.
Review logging and retention settings.
Document data residency for every downstream hop.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for sensitive classes.
